official_meaning: Grades 11-12 / the NEB Grade 12 qualification
common_usage: The single most common Nepali phrasing for school completion
disambiguating_question: Which board issued it - NEB, or Cambridge/IB?

official_meaning: Classes 11-12 / Class 12 completion
common_usage: Universal Indian shorthand for school completion
disambiguating_question: Which board? Which stream and subjects?

official_meaning: PRE-2016: the Grade 10 school-leaving exam. In NQF/post-2016 policy language: the GRADE 12 exam
common_usage: Pre-2016 speakers mean Grade 10; NQF documents mean Grade 12
disambiguating_question: Which grade, and which year did you sit it?
notes: Both readings are legitimate. Never resolve a bare 'SLC' without the year and grade.

official_meaning: Secondary Education Examination, end of Grade 10
disambiguating_question: Did you go on to Grades 11-12?
notes: NOT a university-entry qualification.

official_meaning: Very often a Grade 11-12 institution ('+2 college'); can also be a university-affiliated higher-education campus
common_usage: Students say 'college' for the place they did +2
disambiguating_question: What qualification did the college award, and which university awarded it?
notes: Highest-frequency Nepal terminology trap.

official_meaning: Either a Grades 11-12 (intermediate/higher-secondary) college OR a National University-affiliated degree college
disambiguating_question: What qualification did the college award, and which university awarded it?
notes: ~1,688 colleges are affiliated to National University.

official_meaning: 'Junior college' (Maharashtra) and 'PU college' (Karnataka) mean CLASSES 11-12; otherwise a higher-education college
disambiguating_question: Junior/PU college, or a degree college? Which university awarded the degree?
notes: 45,473 colleges award degrees on behalf of ~1,168 universities.

official_meaning: Usually a further education or sixth-form college (post-16, not higher education); in Scotland an FE/HE college; in Oxford/Cambridge/Durham/London a constituent college of a university
disambiguating_question: What qualification did it award, and who awarded it?
notes: Four distinct senses within the UK alone.

official_meaning: A career-focused post-secondary institution, distinct from a university
disambiguating_question: Which institution? What credential - certificate, diploma, advanced diploma, or degree?

official_meaning: Higher education generally - often used interchangeably with 'university'
disambiguating_question: Two-year or four-year? What degree?
notes: THE OPPOSITE of the Nepal/Bangladesh/UK senses. 'College' in the US means higher education.

official_meaning: AMBIGUOUS: a 3-year polytechnic Diploma in Engineering (after Class 10); an NEP Undergraduate Diploma (2 years, 80 credits, NHEQF 5); a Post-Graduate Diploma (1 year, 40 credits, NHEQF 6); or a PGDM
disambiguating_question: After Class 10, after Class 12, or after a bachelor's degree?
notes: Four distinct meanings.

official_meaning: Most likely a CTEVT 3-year Diploma taken INSTEAD OF Grades 11-12
common_usage: Also used for university postgraduate diplomas
disambiguating_question: CTEVT or a university PGD? After SEE or after Grade 12?

official_meaning: A 4-year BTEB Diploma (Engineering / Agriculture / Medical Technology) at BNQF Level 6 - a level ABOVE the HSC
disambiguating_question: Which field? BTEB-affiliated?
notes: 4 years - LONGER than India's or Nepal's 3-year diplomas.

official_meaning: An AQF Level 5 qualification, awardable by EITHER a VET provider (RTO/TAFE) OR a higher education provider
disambiguating_question: From a TAFE/RTO or a university?

official_meaning: DipHE (FHEQ 5), HND (FHEQ 5), Graduate Diploma (FHEQ 6), or Postgraduate Diploma (FHEQ 7) - all defined levels
disambiguating_question: Which diploma exactly?

official_meaning: A translated Chinese credential rendered as 'Diploma' may be the GRADUATION CERTIFICATE of a 4-5 year benke (undergraduate) programme
disambiguating_question: How many years was the programme? Do you also have a degree certificate?
notes: 'A Benke Certificate of Graduation is often translated as a Diploma'. The REVERSE of the South Asian trap.

official_meaning: THE CERTIFICATE DOCUMENT ITSELF - for a high school diploma or a degree parchment. NOT a sub-degree qualification level
disambiguating_question: What qualification does the diploma certify?
notes: Five-way trap across the eight countries.

official_meaning: AMBIGUOUS: a pre-NEP 3-year specialised single-subject honours degree (120 credits, NHEQF 5.5) OR the NEP 4-year Bachelor's (Honours) (160 credits, NHEQF 6)
disambiguating_question: How many years, and how many total credits?
notes: 'Honours' in pre-NEP India denoted specialisation, NOT an extra year.

official_meaning: A 4-year bachelor's degree, 140 credits, BNQF Level 7 (contrasted with a 3-year 'Pass' degree, 120 credits)
disambiguating_question: How many years? Honours or Pass?
notes: A 4-year degree may be 'with or without honours' - duration and credits are more reliable than the label.

official_meaning: A Bachelor Honours Degree at AQF LEVEL 8 - a LEVEL ABOVE Bachelor Degree (AQF 7), at the same level as a Graduate Certificate/Diploma
disambiguating_question: Integrated (4-year) or a standalone honours year? What class?
notes: NOT structurally the same as a South Asian 'Honours' bachelor's.

official_meaning: A Bachelor Degree with Honours, classified 1st / 2.1 / 2.2 / 3rd. A Bachelor (Ordinary)/Pass degree has NO classification
disambiguating_question: What classification did you get? If none, was it an Ordinary/Pass degree?

official_meaning: An UNDERGRADUATE degree - a bachelor-level qualification titled 'Master of Arts'
disambiguating_question: Which university awarded it?
notes: Arguably the highest-risk naming trap in UK education. UK ENIC: 'In the Universities of Aberdeen, Edinburgh, Glasgow and St Andrews in Scotland, undergraduate degrees are titled MA (Master of Arts) or MA (Master of Arts) (Hons).'

official_meaning: A 2-3 year, 'more practically-oriented' higher-education programme yielding a GRADUATION CERTIFICATE BUT NO BACHELOR'S DEGREE
common_usage: Students may describe it in English as 'university' or 'college diploma'
disambiguating_question: How many years was the programme? Do you have a degree certificate (学位证书) as well as a graduation certificate (毕业证书)?
notes: Characterising a 3-year zhuanke against foreign qualifications is CONTESTED among credential evaluators. Describe it, do not level it.

official_meaning: A 4-5 year undergraduate programme yielding a graduation certificate AND a bachelor's degree certificate
disambiguating_question: Do you have BOTH documents?

term: 毕业证书 / 学位证书
official_meaning: Graduation certificate (programme completion) / Degree certificate (degree conferral) - TWO SEPARATE DOCUMENTS, verified separately
common_usage: 'it is possible to hold a graduation certificate without a degree certificate, and vice versa'
disambiguating_question: Do you have both a graduation certificate and a degree certificate?
notes: THE non-negotiable China question. A 4-year programme completed without degree conferral yields a graduation certificate only.

official_meaning: Higher Secondary Certificate - CLASS 12 in several Indian state boards
disambiguating_question: Which COUNTRY, and which board?
notes: 'HSC' also means Bangladesh's national Class 12 qualification. Establish the country first.

official_meaning: Higher Secondary Certificate - the NATIONAL Class 12 examination, BNQF Level 5
disambiguating_question: Which COUNTRY, and which board?
notes: Not the same as an Indian state-board HSC.

official_meaning: Higher School Certificate - NSW's senior secondary certificate
disambiguating_question: Which country?
notes: A THIRD meaning of 'HSC' across these eight countries.

official_meaning: Secondary School Certificate - CLASS 10 in several Indian state boards
disambiguating_question: Which country, and which board?

official_meaning: Secondary School Certificate - the NATIONAL Class 10 examination, BNQF Level 3
disambiguating_question: Which country, and which board?

official_meaning: Class 10 completion
common_usage: Common in North India and on older certificates
disambiguating_question: Which board? Which year?
notes: NOT a school-leaving qualification for higher education.

official_meaning: Class 12
disambiguating_question: Which board?

official_meaning: The old 2-year post-SLC certificate under Tribhuvan University's certificate level
disambiguating_question: Which awarding body, and which year?
notes: Superseded by NEB Grades 11-12.

official_meaning: Proficiency Certificate Level - TU's 2-3 year certificate level, largely phased out
common_usage: Technical PCL became the CTEVT Diploma
disambiguating_question: Which awarding body and year?

official_meaning: Pre-University Course, second year = Class 12

region_scope: England and Wales vs Northern Ireland
official_meaning: ENGLAND/WALES: the first A-level year (Key Stage 5). NORTHERN IRELAND: the GCSE year (Key Stage 4)
disambiguating_question: Which UK nation?
notes: NI year numbering is OFFSET BY ONE from England's. NI Year 12 = England Year 11.

official_meaning: A GCSE grade sitting BETWEEN C and B, introduced in NI in 2019
disambiguating_question: (Its presence itself identifies NI, 2019 or later)
notes: Northern Ireland ONLY. Reading C* as a 'starred fail' or as equal to C would be a material error.

official_meaning: The year before Grade 1, age ~5
disambiguating_question: Which country?

official_meaning: NSW/ACT: the FIRST YEAR OF SCHOOL. Victoria and elsewhere: a PRE-SCHOOL year
disambiguating_question: Which state?
notes: Real Australian internal ambiguity.

official_meaning: The fifth and final year of Québec secondary school - 'corresponds to grade 11 in other jurisdictions'
disambiguating_question: Did you go on to CEGEP?
notes: 11 years of schooling, not 12.

official_meaning: Collège d'enseignement général et professionnel - 'encompasses grade 12 from high school and the first year of university'
disambiguating_question: Pre-university (2 years) or technical (3 years)? Do you hold a DEC?
notes: No counterpart anywhere else in Canada.

official_meaning: Diplôme d'études collégiales / Diploma of College Studies - the CEGEP award
disambiguating_question: Which stream?
notes: Named in the CDQF alongside the secondary school diploma as a bachelor's-entry qualification.

official_meaning: 'Considered to be BACHELOR'S PROGRAMS IN ACADEMIC STANDING', though they 'yield degrees with other nomenclature'
disambiguating_question: How many years of prior degree-level study?
notes: CDQF, 2007. CONTRAST the UK, where the equivalents are FHEQ 7 (master's level).

term: MB BS / MB ChB / BDS / BVSc
official_meaning: 'Primary qualifications (or first degrees) in medicine, dentistry and veterinary science' at MASTER'S LEVEL, Bologna second cycle
notes: CONTRAST Canada, where MD/DDS are bachelor's-level in academic standing.

official_meaning: Professional doctorates entered AFTER a bachelor's degree. Because the US has no qualifications framework, NO US LEVEL CAN BE STATED
disambiguating_question: How many credits? What prior degree?
notes: Three English-speaking systems, three different placements for structurally similar qualifications.

official_meaning: Reportedly classified as Masters Degree (Extended) at AQF Level 9 - NOT doctorates
notes: The AQF 'Masters (Extended)' type at AQF 9 with a 3-4 year volume IS confirmed; which qualifications fall in it was not verified.

official_meaning: MEng, MChem, MPhys - undergraduate ENTRY but reaching master's level
notes: NOT a bachelor's degree despite undergraduate entry.

official_meaning: Graduate Certificate/Diploma = FHEQ 6 (BACHELOR'S level). Postgraduate Certificate/Diploma = FHEQ 7 (MASTER'S level)
disambiguating_question: Graduate or Postgraduate?
notes: A subtle and consequential UK distinction.

official_meaning: Australian Tertiary Admission Rank - 'a RANK, not a mark or score', 0.00-99.95, the holder's percentile position in the age cohort
disambiguating_question: Which jurisdiction and year?
notes: 'An ATAR of 70 doesn't mean you got 70 percent - it means that you're in the top 30 percent.' MUST NOT be converted.

official_meaning: SCHOOL (SSC/HSC): a 5.00 scale. UNIVERSITY: typically a 4.00 scale
disambiguating_question: Which document? Which scale maximum?
notes: The same student legitimately holds two GPAs on two different scales.

official_meaning: BOTH are 4.0 scales, but with DIFFERENT step patterns: NEB school uses 0.4 steps (4.0/3.6/3.2); universities use US-style steps (4.0/3.7/3.3)
disambiguating_question: Which document? Which institution?
notes: Two structurally different 4.0 scales.

official_meaning: Most Australian universities use a 7-POINT GPA (HD=7, D=6, C=5, P=4, F=0)
disambiguating_question: Out of what maximum?
notes: NOT a 4.0 scale. Distinct from WAM.

official_meaning: Weighted Average Mark - a percentage-based weighted average, used for Honours admission and scholarship ranking
disambiguating_question: GPA or WAM?
notes: NOT the same as GPA.

official_meaning: NO national scale: 4.0, 4.3, 4.33, 9-point, 12-point and percentage systems all exist, varying by province AND institution
disambiguating_question: Which university, and what is the maximum?
notes: A '3.7' could be near-perfect on 4.0, strong on 4.3, or middling on 9- or 12-point.

official_meaning: A GPA including bonus points for Honors (+0.5) and AP/IB (+1.0) courses - CAN EXCEED 4.0
disambiguating_question: High school or college? Weighted or unweighted?
notes: 'College registrars report the unweighted GPA on official transcripts.' A GPA above 4.0 is a high-school weighted figure.

official_meaning: A 10-POINT cumulative grade point average (not 4.0)
disambiguating_question: Which institution? Does the university issue a conversion certificate?
notes: No national CGPA-to-percentage formula exists.

official_meaning: A result below the reporting threshold - replaced 'fail' in the letter-grading era
disambiguating_question: Has a grade-increment exam been taken since?

official_meaning: An NEB re-sit examination to improve a subject grade
disambiguating_question: Does the certificate year differ from the first attempt?

official_meaning: A re-sit for a failed subject (compartment) or to improve a passing score (improvement)
disambiguating_question: Does the certificate year differ from the first attempt?

official_meaning: The Nepali calendar used on documents. BS is approximately AD + 56/57; BS 2081 = 2024/25
disambiguating_question: (Convert BS to AD before reading any date)
notes: A certificate dated '2078' or '2081' is a BS year, not AD.

official_meaning: Nepal's official terms for PUBLIC and PRIVATE schools respectively
notes: Both sit the same NEB examinations and receive the same certificate.

official_meaning: ALIYA: BMEB-governed, issuing Dakhil/Alim with formal SSC/HSC equivalency. QAWMI: a separate non-government religious system OUTSIDE BMEB
disambiguating_question: Aliya (BMEB) or Qawmi?
notes: Do NOT assume BMEB equivalency for a Qawmi qualification.

official_meaning: RECOGNISED BODY: has degree-awarding powers. LISTED BODY: delivers courses leading to ANOTHER body's degrees
disambiguating_question: Which institution AWARDED the degree?

official_meaning: A college that TEACHES but whose degrees are AWARDED BY the affiliating university
disambiguating_question: Which university awarded the degree?
notes: India: 45,473 colleges / ~1,168 universities. Bangladesh: ~1,688 NU-affiliated colleges.

official_meaning: An affiliated college granted autonomy over curriculum and assessment - it SETS ITS OWN pass marks and CGPA thresholds
notes: NHEQF: 'The universities or the autonomous colleges can decide on the grade or percentage of marks required to pass'.

official_meaning: Designated Learning Institution - 'a school approved by a provincial or territorial government to host international students'
notes: A letter of acceptance from a DLI is needed for a study permit.

official_meaning: Educational Credential Assessment - required for SKILLED MIGRATION (e.g. Express Entry), NOT for admission
notes: Never tell a student they need an ECA to STUDY in Canada.

official_meaning: The MOE-authorised credential verification institution (CSSD) and its portal (CHSI). Since August 2022 the SOLE official portal for verifying both graduation and degree certificates
notes: Also verifies senior high school certificates and provincial examination results.

official_meaning: Accredited by an accreditor RECOGNISED BY the U.S. Secretary of Education and/or CHEA
disambiguating_question: Is the accreditor USDE/CHEA-recognised? (Check CHEA's directories or ED's DAPIP)
notes: 'Unaccredited' is a real and occasionally failed test in the US, unlike in most other systems.

official_meaning: Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students - a course must be CRICOS-registered for a student visa
notes: Register updates monthly.

official_meaning: Competency certificates at BNQF Levels 1-6. SSC (Voc) confers SSC + NSC 3; HSC (Voc)/(BMT) confers HSC + NSC 5
disambiguating_question: Do you hold both certificates?
notes: Distinctive DUAL certification design.

official_meaning: 1st/2nd/3rd/4th year of EITHER high school OR a bachelor's degree
disambiguating_question: High school or college?

official_meaning: The institution delivering CLASSES 11-12
disambiguating_question: (Not higher education)

official_meaning: A two-year / community college
disambiguating_question: Which country?
notes: Opposite level to the Indian sense.

term: A-Levels / O-Levels taken outside the UK
official_meaning: UK-LINKED INTERNATIONAL qualifications (International A level, IGCSE, Cambridge GCE O level) - treated by UK ENIC as a DISTINCT CATEGORY from domestic UK GCSEs/A levels
disambiguating_question: Which awarding body, and in which country was it taken?
notes: Do NOT interpret on the local national grading scale, and do NOT assume identity with the domestic UK qualification.

term: IB Diploma taken in any of the eight countries
official_meaning: An INTERNATIONAL qualification from the IBO - not a domestic qualification of the country where it was taken
disambiguating_question: Which awarding body?
notes: Applies in all eight countries in this research.
